title: DLP-LoRA: Efficient Task-Specific LoRA Fusion with a Dynamic, Lightweight Plugin for Large Language Models

contributions.purpose: Enable dynamic, context-driven fusion of multiple task-specific LoRAs without manual pre-selection or retraining when tasks change, while remaining lightweight and easily adaptable to new domains.
contributions.mechanism: DLP-LoRA, a dynamic lightweight plugin: a 4-layer mini-MLP module (~5M parameters) trained once for sentence-level task classification, which selects and fuses multiple LoRAs using top-p sampling strategies.
contributions.evaluation: Plugin is ~5M parameters vs ~26M for a typical token-level gating method on LLaMA-3 8B with 100 LoRAs; trained once at sentence level.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce DLP-LoRA, a dynamic and lightweight plugin for multi-LoRA selection and fusion that is fast to train and easily adaptable to new domains.

contributions.purpose: Reduce the inference-time overhead of multi-LoRA fusion, which token-level MoE gating (e.g. MeteoRA) inflates by routing at every attention/MLP layer.
contributions.mechanism: Sentence-level (rather than token-level) LoRA selection and fusion, leveraging parallel CUDA acceleration and GEMM optimisation by removing per-token independence constraints; LoRAs stored as contiguous tensors in HBM.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves less than twice the inference time of single-LoRA inference, outperforming token-level MoE gating routers in efficiency.
contributions.source_quote: By employing sentence-level multi-LoRA selection and fusion, DLP-LoRA leverages parallel CUDA acceleration, achieving less than twice the inference time compared to single LoRA inference and outperforming token-level MoE gating routers in efficiency.

contributions.purpose: Empirically validate DLP-LoRA across a broad set of tasks and composite (multi-task) settings.
contributions.mechanism: Extensive evaluation across 26 tasks spanning multiple-choice questions (MCQ) and question answering (QA), across different LLM backbones, comparing to single-task LoRA and composite settings.
contributions.evaluation: Average accuracy 92.34% on multiple-choice datasets; significant BLEU/ROUGE improvements on QA; performance comparable to single-task LoRA models and improved accuracy/ROUGE under composite task settings.
contributions.source_quote: Through extensive evaluations on 26 tasks including MCQ and QA, DLP-LoRA achieves performance comparable to single-task LoRA models and significantly improves accuracy and ROUGE metrics under composite task settings.

self_declared_provenance.quote: MeteoRA (Xu et al., 2024) introduces a token-level gating network to all attention and MLP layers for dynamic LoRA fusion ... existing LoRA mixture strategies like MeteoRA focus on token-level Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) gating across all attention heads and MLP layers, which significantly increases inference time ... This suggests that token-level LoRA MoE might be unnecessary and computationally inefficient.

some existing works also proposed sentence-level routing, for instance Polytropon (Ponti et al., 2023) and FLix (Lin et al., 2024a). However, Flix mainly focuses on multilingual task settings and Polytropon mainly explores the encoder-decoder architecture. It is unclear whether those works can maintain superior inference efficiency when loading high volumes of LoRAs.

Huang et al. (2023) introduced LoRAHub, a framework that combines existing fine-tuned LoRAs using a learnable weighted sum ... S-LoRA (Sheng et al., 2023) emphasises unified memory pool design to manage dynamic LoRA weights.

notes: Author-declared result for C3 is a comparable/tie signal: DLP-LoRA 'achieves performance comparable to single-task LoRA models' (i.e. does not clearly beat individually specialized LoRAs), with gains mainly under composite/multi-task settings. Efficiency framed relative to single-LoRA (<2x) rather than absolute speedup. Paper was rejected. No explicit negative result but the 'comparable to single-task' framing is a notable non-improvement caveat.
